ground_truth_question: What does the India IT Mobility Policy cover, and what is its purpose?
ground_truth_answer: The India IT Mobility Policy sets out the process for handling BCG laptops, tech setup assets, and IT accessories when employees move between India and other BCG systems, whether for a temporary assignment or a permanent relocation. It is designed to ensure compliance, enable proper asset tracking, and provide clarity to both employees and IT on the actions required before, during, and after a transfer.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: This policy defines the process for handling BCG laptops, tech setup assets, and IT accessories when employees transfer between India and other BCG systems, either temporarily or permanently. It ensures compliance, proper asset tracking, and clarity for both employees and IT.

ground_truth_question: I’m going on a temporary transfer of less than 12 months—can I carry my India‑issued laptop to the host country?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. For temporary transfers of under 12 months, employees are permitted to carry their India‑issued laptop to the host country. No additional laptop is issued for this situation under the policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Employees may carry their India-issued laptop to the host country.

ground_truth_question: If my India‑issued laptop develops a technical problem while I’m on a temporary transfer, what should I do with the device?
ground_truth_answer: If your India‑issued laptop encounters technical issues during a temporary transfer, you must bring the faulty device back and return it to India Local IT when you return. The host country is not expected to take possession of the device during the temporary assignment.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: In case of technical issues, the faulty laptop must be brought back and returned to India Local IT upon return.

ground_truth_question: My temporary transfer later becomes permanent. What is required regarding my laptop?
ground_truth_answer: If a temporary transfer changes to a permanent move, you must return your India‑issued laptop to India Local IT. The policy also states that if the laptop is not returned, the laptop’s value plus applicable taxes will be recovered from your final settlement.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: If the transfer type changes to permanent, the laptop must be returned to India Local IT. Failure to return the laptop will result in recovery of the laptop value + taxes from final settlement.

ground_truth_question: What are the financial consequences if I do not return my laptop when required after a transfer change?
ground_truth_answer: If you fail to return your laptop when the policy requires it—such as when a temporary transfer converts to a permanent one—the full laptop value plus taxes will be recovered from your final settlement.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Failure to return the laptop will result in recovery of the laptop value + taxes from final settlement.

ground_truth_question: Who is responsible for notifying IT when an employee’s transfer type changes?
ground_truth_answer: Human Resources (HR) is responsible for informing India Local IT when a transfer type changes. This ensures IT can take the necessary asset actions promptly.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: HR must inform India Local IT if transfer type changes.

ground_truth_question: On a temporary transfer, can I keep tech setup assets or accessories such as a display converter or headset?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. During temporary transfers, employees may retain tech setup assets and accessories, with the explicit exception of mobile connectivity items. SIM cards and mobile Wi‑Fi (MiFi) devices are handled separately under the policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Tech setup assets and accessories (except SIM cards and MiFi devices) may be retained.

ground_truth_question: Do I need to return my Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) card and mobile Wi‑Fi (MiFi) device before departing on a temporary transfer?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. SIM cards and MiFi devices must be returned before departure when you are on a temporary transfer. These items are not eligible for retention.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: SIM cards and MiFi devices must be returned before departure.

ground_truth_question: If a temporary transfer later becomes permanent, what is the rule for tech setup items and accessories?
ground_truth_answer: If a temporary transfer later changes to a permanent move, all tech setup items must be returned. Retention is only permitted if you pay the depreciated value plus taxes.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: If transfer type later changes to permanent, all tech setup items must be returned or retained by paying the depreciated value + taxes.

ground_truth_question: For a long‑term transfer of more than 12 months, what must I do with my India‑issued laptop before I leave?
ground_truth_answer: Before departing on a long‑term transfer, you must return your India‑issued laptop to India Local IT. This ensures the proper hand‑off of equipment prior to issuance in the host country.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Employees must return their laptop to India Local IT before leaving.

ground_truth_question: When I relocate long‑term, how will I receive a new laptop and how will my data be restored?
ground_truth_answer: For long‑term transfers, the host country’s Local IT will issue a new laptop. Your data will be restored through OneDrive, so you do not need to manually migrate your files.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Host country Local IT will issue a new laptop and restore data through OneDrive.

ground_truth_question: On a long‑term transfer, must I return items such as SIMs, MiFi devices, or display converters?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. All tech setup items and accessories—including SIM cards, MiFi devices, and display converters—must be returned to India Local IT for a long‑term transfer.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: All tech setup items and accessories (SIM, MiFi, display converters, etc.) must be returned to India Local IT.

ground_truth_question: Can I pay to keep any tech setup assets when moving out of India on a long‑term basis?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. Retention of tech setup assets only is permitted on long‑term transfers if you pay the depreciated value and applicable taxes. This option does not extend to accessories unless otherwise permitted by the policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Retention of tech setup assets (only) is permitted by paying the depreciated value taxes.

ground_truth_question: For a long‑term transfer exception, whose approval is required?
ground_truth_answer: Exceptions in the long‑term transfer context require a valid business justification and approvals from the IT Senior Director (Jagmohan Singh Sehgal) and the India Finance Director (Shailesh Dolas).
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
Exceptions require business justification and approval from:
o IT Senior Director (Jagmohan Singh Sehgal)
o India Finance Director (Shailesh Dolas)

ground_truth_question: During a Leave of Absence (LOA) or secondment, may I retain my laptop?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. Employees may retain their laptop while on a Leave of Absence or secondment. If you later move out of India during this period to join another BCG office, different return rules apply.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Employees may retain their laptop during LOA/secondment.

ground_truth_question: If I move out of India to join another BCG office during my Leave of Absence (LOA) or secondment, what must I do with my laptop?
ground_truth_answer: If you move out of India to join another BCG office during an LOA or secondment, you must return the laptop to India Local IT. The device cannot be retained under this scenario.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
If moving out of India to join another BCG office during this time:
o The laptop must be returned to India Local IT.

ground_truth_question: If I move out of India during a Leave of Absence (LOA) or secondment, what happens to my accessories?
ground_truth_answer: All accessories must be returned when you move out of India to join another BCG office during an LOA or secondment.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
If moving out of India to join another BCG office during this time:
o All accessories must also be returned.

ground_truth_question: While moving to another BCG office during a Leave of Absence (LOA) or secondment, can I retain any tech setup assets by paying for them?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. In this situation, tech setup assets may be retained by paying the depreciated value and taxes, consistent with the policy’s provisions.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
If moving out of India to join another BCG office during this time:
o Tech setup assets may be retained by paying the depreciated value taxes.

ground_truth_question: I am transferring permanently to India and do not have a BCG laptop. Will I be issued one?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. Employees transferring permanently to India will be issued a standard India laptop if they do not already have a BCG laptop.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Employees transferring permanently to India will be issued a standard India laptop if not already holding a BCG laptop.

ground_truth_question: What keyboard layout will come with the laptop issued when I transfer permanently to India?
ground_truth_answer: The laptop issued for a permanent transfer to India will be configured with a standard Indian keyboard.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Issued laptop will have a standard Indian keyboard.

ground_truth_question: What IT enablement equipment comes with the laptop when I transfer permanently to India?
ground_truth_answer: You will receive the standard IT enablement equipment kit, which includes a laptop charger, a wired headset, a privacy screen, and other comparable items.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Employees will also receive the standard IT enablement equipment kit (laptop charger, wired headset, privacy screen, etc.).

ground_truth_question: I’m on a short‑term transfer to India. Will a new laptop be issued to me?
ground_truth_answer: No. Individuals on short‑term or temporary transfers to India will not be issued a new laptop under this policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Individuals on short-term/temporary transfers to India will not be issued a new laptop.

ground_truth_question: If my laptop fails while I’m on a temporary assignment in India, can I get a loaner?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. If your laptop fails while you are temporarily in India, a loaner laptop may be provided, subject to stock availability.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: If their current laptop fails, a loaner laptop may be provided subject to stock.

ground_truth_question: Do I need to return the loaner laptop before I leave India after a temporary assignment?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. Any loaner laptop issued during a temporary transfer to India must be returned before you leave India.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Loaner laptops must be returned before leaving India.

ground_truth_question: What connectivity SIMs will I receive during a temporary transfer to India, and how long is the mobile SIM valid?
ground_truth_answer: You will be issued a data SIM for your laptop and a voice‑and‑data SIM for your mobile phone. The mobile SIM is valid for six months only, after which you must procure your own SIM.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
Individuals will be issued:
o Data SIM for laptop
o Voice & data SIM for mobile (valid for 6 months only; individual must then procure their own SIM)

ground_truth_question: Will international roaming be enabled on the SIMs provided to me during a temporary transfer to India?
ground_truth_answer: No. International roaming will not be activated on the SIMs issued for temporary transfers to India.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: No international roaming will be activated on these SIMs.

ground_truth_question: Should I use the provided SIMs for international calls while I am temporarily in India?
ground_truth_answer: No. You are advised not to make international calls using these SIMs issued for temporary transfers to India.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Individuals are advised not to make international calls using these SIMs.

ground_truth_question: Are temporary staff, including those categorized as COS, entitled to tech setup accessories when they are in India temporarily?
ground_truth_answer: No. Temporary and COS staff are not entitled to tech setup accessories under this policy.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Temporary/COS staff are not entitled to tech setup accessories.

ground_truth_question: If we need to deviate from these processes for a specific case, what approvals are required across the policy?
ground_truth_answer: Any exception to the policy requires a valid business justification and approvals from the IT Senior Director (Jagmohan Singh Sehgal), the India Finance Director (Shailesh Dolas), and the HR Head of Function (Akshit Shah). All three approvals are required.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
Any exception to the above processes requires:
• Valid business justification, and approval from:
o IT Senior Director (Jagmohan Singh Sehgal)
o India Finance Director (Shailesh Dolas)
o HR Head of Function (Akshit Shah)

ground_truth_question: What is the difference between exceptions for long‑term transfers and exceptions to the overall policy?
ground_truth_answer: Under the long‑term transfer section, exceptions require a business justification and approvals from the IT Senior Director and the India Finance Director. For exceptions to the overall policy, approvals are required from all three roles—the IT Senior Director, the India Finance Director, and the HR Head of Function—based on a valid business justification.
exact_excerpt_from_policy:
Transfers More Than 12 Months (Long-Term Transfers)
• Exceptions require business justification and approval from:
o IT Senior Director (Jagmohan Singh Sehgal)
o India Finance Director (Shailesh Dolas)
Exceptions
Any exception to the above processes requires:
• Valid business justification, and approval from:
o IT Senior Director (Jagmohan Singh Sehgal)
o India Finance Director (Shailesh Dolas)
o HR Head of Function (Akshit Shah)

ground_truth_question: For a long‑term transfer, do I specifically need to return my display converters?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. Display converters are explicitly listed among the accessories that must be returned to India Local IT for long‑term transfers out of India.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: All tech setup items and accessories (SIM, MiFi, display converters, etc.) must be returned to India Local IT.

ground_truth_question: On a temporary transfer of under 12 months, may I keep my privacy screen?
ground_truth_answer: Yes. A privacy screen is a tech setup accessory, and the policy permits retention of such assets during a temporary transfer. The only items explicitly excluded from retention in this scenario are SIM cards and MiFi devices, which must be returned before departure.
exact_excerpt_from_policy: Tech setup assets and accessories (except SIM cards and MiFi devices) may be retained.
